entry.title: fix(capture): put /ws/hook behind the capture gate (#112)
entry.content:
fix(capture): put /ws/hook behind the capture gate (#112)

The inbound hook websocket was the one live capture source that neither
respected the gate nor re-resolved the database. Every other source —
clipboard, the outbound hook client, the region watcher, the hotkey — goes
through gate.ingest(); this one wrote straight through, so a line arriving
during a backup restore landed in the database being replaced.

It now answers {"ok": false, "error": "paused"} instead of dropping the line
silently: the peer is a program, and a silent success is worse for it than a
refusal. The session is resolved per message rather than once per connection,
because a Textractor connection stays open for a whole evening.

The regression test for the database asserts how many times app.state.db is
resolved, not where the row lands. SQLite reconnects a disposed engine to the
same path, so a captured handle still writes the row on macOS — the real
damage is a connection held open across the file swap, which does not
reproduce here. Counting resolutions is what actually separates the two
implementations, and both new tests fail without this change.

Closes #89

Assisted-by: Claude Code (Opus 5)

entry.title: fix(system): restore and long jobs must not write together (#113)
entry.content:
fix(system): restore and long jobs must not write together (#113)

JMdict install, pitch install, KANJIDIC import and the FSRS optimizer each
open one session and hold it for minutes. Nothing stopped a backup restore
from disposing and replacing the database underneath them.

The gate already coordinates live capture against restore, so it gains the
other half rather than a second primitive: a job claims the database on the
request thread, so the caller gets a real error instead of a job that reports
failure later, and releases it on the worker thread that ends it. Restore
refuses outright while a claim is held rather than waiting — a JMdict import
runs for minutes, and blocking a restore that long is not a better outcome
than asking the user to try again.

Jobs still run alongside each other; only restore is exclusive. Mutual
exclusion also removes the stale-handle question for these four, since the
database can no longer be replaced while they hold it.

The claim is released if the thread fails to start. A leaked claim would
refuse every future restore until the process is restarted, which is a worse
failure than the one being fixed.

Closes #91

entry.title: docs: define issue label semantics for agents (#105)
entry.content:
docs: define issue label semantics for agents (#105)

Section 7 told an agent how to consume `agent-ready` but nothing said how to
apply it, so the queue's index was being maintained by habit. Section 8 now
writes the three dimensions down: exactly one type label, readiness, and the
labels that are promises to other people.

The point worth stating plainly is that `agent-ready` is a readiness state
and not a byline. An issue is not ready because an agent wrote it, and a
human can file a vague one; the label answers whether an unattended run can
finish without asking anything, and nothing else.

Writing it down surfaced a contradiction: §7 said a human decides the label,
which would forbid what §8 describes. Resolved by moving the human checkpoint
to where it protects the queue — an agent may classify an issue it opens, but
may not then take that issue, because certifying your own find and building
it leaves no human in the loop at any point.

Two labels are new because the repository already needed them: eight issues
titled `test(...)` and one titled `refactor(...)` were filed as `enhancement`
for want of anywhere better. `japanese` is new too, and that is a bug fix —
the japanese.md template already declared it, GitHub silently ignores labels
that do not exist, so every issue filed through that template arrived with no
label at all.

entry.title: feat(text): import EPUB light novels as sentence lines (#99)
entry.content:
feat(text): import EPUB light novels as sentence lines (#99)

Light novels are the highest signal-to-noise text source there is, and an
EPUB is already structured: following the spine turns a book into chapters of
clean sentences. Ruby readings are kept beside the sentence rather than
concatenated into it -- 食べ物たべもの would wreck tokenization -- and the
import commits in batches, so a 100k-character book finishes without holding
the book in memory.

Bulk imports match duplicates by exact text hash only: the OCR re-capture
heuristics (prefix growth, similarity) would drop a long narration sentence
that differs from its neighbour by one character. That needs create_lines(),
which stages a batch of lines and commits once.

entry.content:
feat(learning): import KANJIDIC2 and show kanji progress (#104)

* feat(learning): import KANJIDIC2 and show kanji progress

Kanji have structure that word lists hide: a Chinese reader wants to know

pass over the terms plus two queries, never one query per character.

entry.title: feat(capture): read bound windows from their own pixels (#102)
entry.content:
feat(capture): read bound windows from their own pixels (#102)

A screen grab reads whatever is on top; the moment another window covers the
game -- or, later, our own overlay sits over it -- the OCR sees the wrong
picture. With a window bound, capture now asks the window to render itself
via PrintWindow(PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT), crops the client area out of the
frame, and treats an all-black answer as failure so the caller still falls
back to the screen grab. REST collect, the hotkey collector and the watcher
all pass the bound window.

Verified on Windows 11 with PARQUET fully covered by the terminal: the screen
grab returned empty text, the window grab read the live line and stored it
with the cropped screenshot. Tests cover the preferred window path, the
fallback and the watcher grabber.

entry.title: feat(capture): keep a rolling media buffer for late backfills (#101)
entry.content:
feat(capture): keep a rolling media buffer for late backfills (#101)

The learner notices a missed word after the line already left the screen, so
keep the last minute of frames (and audio, once a source exists) in memory and
let POST /api/lines/{id}/backfill attach them to a line that already exists:
the most recent frame not later than captured_at, within a configurable
tolerance. A byte cap rather than a count bounds the memory, stopping the
watcher releases it, and the buffer itself never touches the data directory.

entry.title: feat(text): read mokuro output so manga becomes a source (#95)
entry.content:
feat(text): read mokuro output so manga becomes a source (#95)

Manga is a major Japanese-learning medium and mokuro already solves the hard
OCR part; importing its .mokuro volumes turns them into sessions of
page-located lines. The upload accepts only the .mokuro file (no page images),
so imported lines carry a page locator but no screenshot yet; the reader view
will render the text instead.

Field names were checked against mokuro 0.2.5 (master) and its 0.2.0-beta.6
fixture; a mismatch raises bad_mokuro instead of importing half a volume. The
line order stays mokuro's own: the detector sorts each block's lines and keeps
re-sorting while splitting and merging, and re-deriving the order from box
centres tore apart a column the fixture split into two stacked lines.

entry.title: feat(capture): follow the game window instead of fixed screen pixels …
entry.content:
feat(capture): follow the game window instead of fixed screen pixels (#98)

Manual pixel framing breaks the moment the window moves, and games are
windows, not screens. A work can now be bound to a running window (the list
comes from the OS -- process, title, size; nothing is guessed from a game's
name), and its dialogue box is stored relative to the client area, so moving
the window, switching monitors or changing resolution keeps the same box.

The hotkey collector and the region watcher resolve the binding on use, the
watcher once per cycle; the last absolute region stays as a fallback for when
the game is closed. Verified on Windows 11 with PARQUET: OCR read the live
line from the bound dialogue box, collect stored it with a screenshot, and
the watcher captured a line on its own.

entry.title: docs: cover M1's capture surfaces and per-platform install (#97)
entry.content:
docs: cover M1's capture surfaces and per-platform install (#97)

SECURITY.md still described M0's threat model. Since it was written the app
gained three capture surfaces it never mentioned, two of which a
privacy-conscious reader has to be told about before they turn them on: the
global shortcut installs an OS-level keyboard hook that receives events from
every window, and the clipboard watcher polls the clipboard three times a
second and ingests anything short and Japanese, whatever it was copied for.
Screen capture is no longer only the moment you press a shortcut either —
the region watcher runs until stopped.

"Only the JMdict dictionary" was also no longer true: pitch accent data is
fetched from Kanjium, and Yomitan packs, .apkg decks, subtitles and backups
are all parsed from files that usually come off the internet. Said so, and
said plainly that parsing untrusted input is where a bug is most likely.

README assumed a reader who already has uv and Node. The audience is someone
who wants to learn Japanese from a visual novel, so the prerequisites are now
actual per-platform commands, and it says up front that there is no installer
yet rather than letting people look for one. The phone section covers what
actually goes wrong — AP isolation, the firewall prompt, and the fact that
the port has no authentication at all.

Assisted-by: Claude Code (Opus 5)

entry.title: build(package): ship a bundled Windows app and installer (#96)
entry.content:
build(package): ship a bundled Windows app and installer (#96)

Windows users cannot be asked to run Python. make package-windows now builds
the frontend, a PyInstaller onedir bundle and (optionally) an Inno Setup
installer, and then proves the bundle works: the smoke test starts the frozen
exe on a throwaway data dir and checks the SPA, a real Windows OCR round-trip
and tokenization -- exactly the pieces PyInstaller breaks silently. The frozen
SPA lookup now reads sys._MEIPASS instead of walking up from __file__.

PyInstaller stays in its own packaging extra. Signing is scripted (thumbprint
or PFX via KOTOBA_PFX_PASSWORD) but untested: this machine has no certificate.
docs/CODE_SIGNING.md covers certificate sources, CI secrets and the macOS gap.

Measured on Windows 11: bundle 321.8 MB (260 MB is the unidic-lite
dictionary), installer 56.1 MB, install ~7 s, first start 1.6-2.9 s; install,
run and silent uninstall tested for real. macOS .app and notarization are not
part of this change.

entry.title: refactor(models): give every line a locator and a stable order (#88)
entry.content:
refactor(models): give every line a locator and a stable order (#88)

漫画与 EPUB 是文档式的（第几页 + 框 / 第几章 + 偏移），现有流式模型没有位置；「一种格式加两列」会让 `Line` 每接一种内容就迁移一次。`Line` 增加 `locator_json`（`{"kind": …}`，kind 必填）与索引列 `ord`（作品内稳定顺序），`start_ms`/`end_ms`/`position_json` 原样保留；`schemas/lines.line_locator()` 在缺少 `locator_json` 时从旧字段合成（time / region），老数据照样可读。字幕导入成为第一个写入方（`kind="time"` + cue 序号 ord）。列表与词条时间线排序改为 `ord` 优先、`captured_at` 兜底——导入整本书时时间戳几乎相同，不能再靠它排序。ADR 0003 记录取舍：为什么不按格式加列、不用多态表、选 JSON，以及代价（locator 内部字段无法建索引）。

**验证**：`make check` 全绿（exit=0）：后端 ruff/format、`pytest` 175 passed + 1 skipped（本 PR 新增 5 条），前端 lint/typecheck/30 tests/build 通过；Alembic 自动生成只含这两列 + 索引，逐行看过（无 `UTCDateTime` 坑），在 dev 库 `upgrade head` 验证单一 head。测试：旧字段（time/region）合成 locator、`locator_json` 优先、坏 JSON 返回 None、`ord` 决定列表顺序（captured_at 相同时）、字幕导入写 locator 与 ord。

**未能验证**：漫画/EPUB 的实际 locator 形态要等各自导入器；前端只是类型补齐，没有 UI 变化。

Closes #51

entry.title: feat(capture): collect the current line from a global hotkey (#85)
entry.content:
feat(capture): collect the current line from a global hotkey (#85)

A global hotkey collects the current line without leaving the game: one
configurable combination (default Ctrl+Shift+S) screenshots the saved region,
OCRs it and stores the line, and failures -- no saved region, a backup restore
in flight, macOS missing Accessibility -- show up in the settings status
instead of failing silently. pynput is a new base dependency, imported lazily
so a headless server still boots.

Windows testing found two things only a real machine shows: pynput ignores
synthetic input, so the check needs a human press; and a held Ctrl turns a
letter into its control character before matching (a real Ctrl+S arrives as
DC3), so control characters are normalised back first. Verified on Windows 11
with the built-in OCR: a real Ctrl+Shift+S collected the rendered line with
its screenshot. The matching check skips where no keyboard backend exists.

entry.title: fix(dict): tell frequency tables apart from dictionaries in settings …
entry.content:
fix(dict): tell frequency tables apart from dictionaries in settings (#87)

设置页的词典列表已经不再受 `installed`（那是 JMdict 的标志）门槛限制，但导入时两种包都写成 `kind="yomitan"`：频率表显示成「2 条」的词典，用户会以为导了一部只有两个词的词典。频率导入改存 `kind="yomitan-freq"`，且只替换同 kind 的同名记录（同名的词条词典不再被频率导入删掉）；加一个**数据迁移**给拆分前导入的行按「有 term_frequencies、无 dict_entries」重标；设置页每行显示类型标签与真实计数单位（`N 条词条` / `N 条频率`），空状态文案改为「尚未安装 JMdict，也还没有导入其他词典」，不再把用户已导入的东西说没。JMdict 安装按钮与 `installed` 语义不动。

**验证**：`make check` 全绿（exit=0）：后端 ruff/format、`pytest` 170 passed + 1 skipped（本 PR 新增 2 条，含同名词条+频率共存的回归），前端 eslint/prettier/`vue-tsc`/30 tests（新增 2 条 vitest）/build 通过。数据迁移在干净 dev 库上 `upgrade head` 验证单一 head；迁移测试覆盖的是新导入的 kind 与共存场景。前端 vitest 覆盖 `dictionaryKindLabel`/`dictionaryCountLabel`/`dictionaryListShows`（installed=false 但列表非空时仍渲染）。

entry.title: fix(dict): attribute glosses to the dictionary they came from (#84)
entry.content:
fix(dict): attribute glosses to the dictionary they came from (#84)

日中词典的中文释义被标成「英文释义」并署名 JMdict——M2 的全部意义就是让中文母语者导入社区日中词典，这样等于把他导的东西署名给一部他没装的词典，对 CC-BY-SA 的词典是实打实的署名错误。查词 DTO 现在带上 `dict_title` / `dict_kind`（`lookup()` join Dictionary）；收件箱编辑器的字段改成中性的「词典释义」并在旁边标出来源词典标题，`sense.origin` 通过 `senseOrigin()` 记录真实来源（标题 ≤16 字符用标题，否则退回 kind，因为 origin 列是 16 位），不再写死 `jmdict`；词条页的角标按每条 sense 的 origin 显示（`originLabel()`：JMdict/自填/Yomitan 词典/自定义标题）。已存数据不做迁移。**不猜语言**是刻意的：词典包没有可靠的语言标记（issue 明确划出范围）。

**验证**：`make check` 全绿（exit=0）：后端 ruff/format、`pytest` 169 passed + 1 skipped（本 PR 新增 2 条），前端 eslint/prettier/`vue-tsc`/28 tests（新增 2 条 vitest）/build 通过。后端测试：导入自造 Yomitan 词典后 `GET /api/dict/lookup?q=水` 返回 `dict_title="测试词典"`、`dict_kind="yomitan"`；JMdict fixture 查词返回其自身标题与 kind。前端 vitest：`senseOrigin`（短标题用标题、超长退回 kind、中文释义记 user）、`originLabel` 映射。

**未能验证**：没有用真实日中词典包验证标题长度/内容形态；浏览器里没实际点过；旧数据（`origin="jmdict"` 的 Yomitan 释义）会继续显示 JMdict，直到用户重新建那条 sense。

entry.title: feat(review): show pitch on the card back and quiz it (#83)
entry.content:
feat(review): show pitch on the card back and quiz it (#83)

音高数据进来了就得用得上。卡面**背面**对每个已记录音高画一条 `PitchLine`（纯 CSS/SVG，无第三方库）：按 mora 分段（拗音合一拍），高拍画线、降位断开、平板一路到底，并显示型名；**正面不显示**（reading 卡若在正面给读音就是泄题）。同一词多个音高全部展示。小测新增 `pitch` 题型：给词与读法、四选一选型（选择在服务端校验），沿用现有 quiz 结构；**没有音高数据时该题型自然不出题**，同一词有多个音高时跳过（答案有歧义）。小测仍走 `mode="session_quiz"`，绝不碰 FSRS 调度（不变量 1，测试里断言卡的状态/到期时间不变）。

entry.title: feat(ui): give the Classical system a motion layer (#79)
entry.content:
feat(ui): give the Classical system a motion layer (#79)

The design held up statically but every state change was a hard cut: the
whole app had exactly one transition (a button background) and not a single
<Transition>. Cards appeared, answers revealed, pages swapped and toasts
vanished all in one frame, which is what made an otherwise careful design
feel rough.

The motion follows the paper-and-ink language rather than the spring-loaded
one most UI kits ship: opacity leads, translation never exceeds 6px, and
everything eases out — paper settles, it does not bounce. Durations are
scaled for a tool someone uses for hours (120/200/320ms), not for a
marketing page.

The reveal is the one deliberate beat. Front and back now cross-fade with
mode="out-in" so the two faces can never share a frame — that is invariant
§5.2 enforced by the transition rather than by hoping. Behind it the four
zones rise in sequence, 70ms apart, so the answer lands before the context
arrives instead of the whole back face dropping at once.

Token ink density encodes learning state, so those colour changes are now
transitions: a word moving from unknown to learning settles instead of
snapping to a different grey.

The existing prefers-reduced-motion block already zeroes every duration
with !important, so this whole layer disables itself there.

Assisted-by: Claude Code (Opus 5)
